PUNJAB CHARITIES (APPEAL) RULES, 2023
[Gazette of Punjab Extraordinary,
27th November, 2023]
No.E&A(HD)14-2/2019(P-II),
dated 21-11-2023.---In exercise of
the powers conferred under section 38 read with section 36 of the Punjab
Charities Act, 2018 (V of 2018), Governor of the Punjab is pleased to make the
following rules:
1. Short title and commencement.-(1) These rules may be cited as the Punjab
Charities (Appeal) Rules, 2023.
(2) They
shall come into force at once.
2. Definitions.- (1) In the rules, unless the subject or context
requires otherwise:
(a) "Act"
means the Punjab Charities Act, 2018 (V of 2018);
(b) "Appellate
Committee" means the Appellate Committee constituted under section 36 of
the Act;
(c) "authorized
representative" means:
(i) in relation to a charity, includes a person authorized in accordance
with the duly registered document of the charity or an advocate entitled to
appear before High Court and is duly authorized by the charity to appear, plead
and act on its behalf before the Appellate Committee;
(ii) in
relation to the Commission, an officer duly authorized by the Commission to
appear, plead and act before the Appellate Committee; and
(iii)
in relation to any other appellant or respondent, a person or an advocate of
High Court who is duly authorized by the appellant or respondent to appear,
plead and act on his behalf before the Appellate Committee.
(d) "Chairperson"
means Chairperson of the Appellate Committee;
(e) "Registrar"
means Registrar of the Appellate Committee appointed by the Commission;
(f) "rules"
means the Punjab Charities (Appeal) Rules, 2023; and
(g) "Schedule" means the
Schedule appended to the rules.
(2) A
word or expression used but not defined in the rules shall have the same
meaning as assigned to it in the Act.
3. Sitting of Appellate Committee.- The Appellate Committee shall hold sitting at such
place as the Chairperson may determine.
4. Filing of appeal.- (1) An appellant may prefer an appeal to the
Appellate Committee within a period of thirty days from the date of passing of
the order or direction by the Commission.
(2) The
memorandum of appeal shall be in such form as set out in Schedule-I and
shall be accompanied by:
(a)
certified copy of the order or direction;
(b)
written authorization in favour of the authorized representative, where
required;
(c)
copies of challans for payment of fee and fine as provided in the Schedule-II;
and
(d) any
other document upon which the appellant has relied upon.
(3) The
memorandum of appeal may be presented in the office of Registrar or sent by
registered post:
Provided
that the memorandum of appeal sent by post shall be deemed to have been
presented on the day it is received in the office of Registrar.
(4) The
memorandum of appeal shall be presented in quadruplicate in the form of paper
book consisting or the original memorandum of appeal and three copies certified
by the appellant or his authorized representative.
(5) The
appellant shall, before filing an appeal, send a copy of memorandum of appeal
to the Commission by registered post and a certificate to this effect shall be
appended with memorandum of appeal.
(6) The
appellant shall, at the time of filing the appeal, deposit the cost of service
of the notice of appeal as provided in Schedule-II in the account of the
Appellate Committee.
(7) In
case a fact contrary to the record is alleged, it shall be stated clearly and
concisely by an affidavit filed with the memorandum of appeal.
(8) In
case the Registrar considers that memorandum of appeal is not filed in
accordance with the rules or incomplete, it may give such directions to the
appellant as may be necessary to remedy the defect in the memorandum of appeal.
(9) In
case an appeal is filed against the order of penalty or fine, the appellant
shall deposit twenty five percent of the penalty or fine so imposed at the time
of filing of appeal.
